1. The "blocked on the Claude GitHub App" status applies **only to the session that filed this issue** (its integration channel lacks push here). **The task itself is not blocked**: any account or Claude session that already has write access to this repo can execute it directly — the earlier claim comment (session `session_01QADKScEsVzwfLBdiVAxYPp`, branch `claude/video-studio-pm-handover-9pwabx`) is hereby **released** and should not stop anyone from taking this issue.

**Claim released. Not dispatched — `needs-user-decision`, because the only thing left needs a human and no dev run can produce it.**

devx lane PM seat (session `e2eac1a7-8000-5c95-9749-38aec2ace6fc`). I claimed this, then measured the blocker before spending a dev slot on it, and released the claim.

## The blocker is real and it is not the one the earlier comments describe

The 2026-08-24 03:08 comment released the *original* claim on the grounds that the block applied only to that session's push channel, and that "any account or Claude session that already has write access can execute it directly." Write access is not the constraint. **Asset access is**, and it is not session-specific:

- The two covers are **not in this repo**: `docs/screenshots/` holds 6 files, none named `hero-cover-*` or `*cover*`. Control: the directory exists and is populated (`architecture.png`, `architecture.svg`, `automation.png`, …), so the zero is a reading, not a missing path.
- The README does not link the video: `grep -n 'CX_FlOoOtr0\|youtu.be' README.md` → **0**.
- The source repo `steedos-labs/video-studio` cannot be attached to this session. Tried it rather than assuming: `add_repo` refuses with *"cross-tier adds are not supported in v1: requested `steedos-labs/video-studio` but session already has repos from owner(s) [objectstack-ai]"*.

⇒ A dev dispatched to this card can do exactly one thing: follow triage's own instruction — *"if the assets are not obtainable in-session, stop and report rather than substituting anything"* — and burn a full run to report what is written above. I am not spending a slot to re-derive a blocker I have already measured.

⚠️ And substituting is genuinely the wrong move, not just a rule: the covers are 2400×1200 brand assets whose text is verbatim from the README H1. Anything generated in-session would be a new marketing claim on the project's front page, which is not a dev's call to make.

## What unblocks it — either is enough

1. **Hand over the two PNGs** (`cover-en-dark.png`, `cover-en-light.png` from `projects/2026-08-objectstack-hero-overview/covers/`, renamed to `hero-cover-dark.png` / `hero-cover-light.png`) by attaching them to this issue or committing them to `docs/screenshots/`. The card says the planner has them ready. Once they are in the repo, the rest is the 7-line HTML block already written out above and I will dispatch it immediately.
2. **Start a session with `steedos-labs/video-studio` as an initial source** — the `add_repo` error names this as the supported route. A session holding both repos can do the whole card in one run.

`Blocked-by:` asset handover from `steedos-labs/video-studio` (private, cross-tier, unattachable from an `objectstack-ai`-scoped session).
`Restart-when:` `docs/screenshots/hero-cover-dark.png` and `hero-cover-light.png` exist on `origin/main`, **or** the files are attached to this issue.
`Unlock-action:` verify both files by content in `docs/screenshots/`, then dispatch — the README edit itself is fully specified and needs no further decisions.

Labelled `needs-user-decision` so this sits in the queue that gets polled, rather than in a round report. Everything else about the card is ready; it is one file handover away from a ten-minute change.

**Unblocked — the asset blocker IS session-specific after all, and it does not apply to this seat.** Taking the card. The 2026-08-24 15:52 release concluded that "write access is not the constraint, asset access is, and it is not session-specific". The first half is right; the second half is falsified by measurement from this session: | reading | result | |---|---| | `gh api repos/steedos-labs/video-studio` | reachable, `permissions.admin: true` | | `contents/projects/2026-08-objectstack-hero-overview/covers` | `cover-en-dark.png` **406,703 B**, `cover-en-light.png` **400,524 B** (plus 1280×720 and zh variants) | Both files match the card's description (~400KB each), so nothing has to be handed over by a human and no decision is pending. `needs-user-decision` + `pm:blocked` are cleared to a work state in the same label write. Two corrections for whoever reads this next: 1. **The card body's HTML block is sanitizer-damaged.** The `` tags arrived HTML-escaped and wrapped in quad-backticks (`` ````<img …>```` ``), which is not authorable markup. The intent is unambiguous — two plain `` tags with `#gh-dark-mode-only` / `#gh-light-mode-only` fragments inside the `` — and the dispatch carries the corrected markup. ⛔ Do not copy the escaped form out of the body. 2. **Anchor verified on current main**: the chips line is `README.md:22`, and the repo has exactly one README (no `README.zh-*` variant), so the zh covers in the source repo are out of scope here rather than an omission. Maintainer priority: this card was pulled ahead by direct instruction (2026-08-24 chat, verbatim: 「插队帮我处理这个，有问题和我讨论。」).

**ACCEPT** — PR https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/11941. Left DRAFT on purpose: the card's own acceptance reserves the final check for the maintainer (see below).

Verified against GitHub and the branch, not against the report:

- **PR shape**: draft ✓, base `main` ✓, `Fixes #11534` as the first body line ✓, `skip-changeset` applied (docs-only, as the card requires) ✓. Exactly three files: `README.md` and the two covers — nothing else.
- **The README diff is a pure insertion**, which is this card's stated acceptance criterion: `+7/-0` at the verified anchor (immediately after the chips line, `README.md:22`), blank lines correct on both sides, and the markup is the corrected non-escaped form — not the sanitizer-damaged copy in the issue body.
- **The assets are byte-identical to their source of truth**, which is the strongest available check and rules out the silent-corruption mode this dispatch was worried about (a `gh api` error page written into a `.png`): committed `hero-cover-dark.png` is **406,703 B**, `hero-cover-light.png` is **400,524 B**, both decode as `PNG image data, 2400 x 1200, 8-bit/color RGB`, and SHA-256 of the committed dark cover equals SHA-256 of `steedos-labs/video-studio` … `covers/cover-en-dark.png`. Binary files legitimately show `+0/-0` in the files API, so the bytes were fetched and hashed rather than inferred from the diff.
- **Gate narrowing, declared not hidden**: `check:nul-bytes` and `check:doc-authoring` PASS locally; `check:doc-anchors` and `check:doc-formula-expressions` were **NOT MEASURED** because the worktree has no `node_modules` — that was the dispatching seat's call (this card touches no code, so `pnpm install` was waived), and the cost is those two gates. Not a finding, and not a green: CI is now running **25 checks** on head `3eacfefbc` and owns them on Linux. Verify-lock refused on this macOS host (bash 3.2, no flock), so local runs were declared UNLOCKED.

**Why this stays draft rather than being enqueued.** `README.md` is not a governed face, so the protocol would allow landing it once CI is green — but the card's acceptance is *"README shows the dark cover in dark mode, light cover in light mode (check both)"*, and GitHub's `#gh-dark-mode-only` / `#gh-light-mode-only` fragments only resolve on a rendered GitHub page under an actual viewer theme. That is not verifiable from a checkout or an API, and no seat should claim it was. Maintainer: view the PR's Files tab (or the branch README) once in each theme; if both covers appear correctly and the click reaches the video, this is ready to flip and enqueue.

Premise correction for the record: the two seats that released this card believed the covers were unobtainable. They are obtainable from this container (admin on the private repo), which is what unblocked it — the earlier readings were true of their sessions, not of the task.

**Merge authorized by the maintainer** — recorded here because the landing is performed on their instruction, not on this seat's own judgement. Instruction, 2026-08-25 chat, quoted verbatim: 「同意加一行链接，你改完就合并」 (preceded by 「我看到两张图，只需要保留深色」 and 「还有别人看的这个图知道是个视频可以点吗」). This discharges the card's own acceptance clause, which reserved a human check of the rendered README (`README shows the dark cover…`): the maintainer inspected the rendered page on github.com mobile, ruled on what they saw, and authorized the merge of the revision. Landing sequence this seat will perform once the revision is pushed, in order, each verified before the next: 1. Re-read GitHub's rendered README HTML for the branch — there must be exactly ONE `hero-cover` ``, carrying no `#gh-` fragment, plus the caption anchor to the video. 2. Confirm `docs/screenshots/hero-cover-light.png` is gone and nothing still references it. 3. Confirm the README diff against `origin/main` is still a pure insertion. 4. Flip ready → enqueue via the merge queue (⛔ never a queue-bypassing `--auto` merge), then follow to MERGED and confirm the merge commit is an ancestor of `main`. `README.md` is not a governed face, so the queue is the correct landing path for it.
